popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book II's Catalogue of Ships — Pheidippus and Antiphus, sons of Thessalus son of Heracles, lead the Coan contingent of thirty ships to Troy.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus keeps Thessalus among Heracles' sons — the Coan king whose name also anchors traditions about Thessaly's eponym.

popCulture.title: Cos (island)
popCulture.description: The Dodecanese island whose Homeric kings descend from Thessalus son of Heracles — the hero-king behind the Coan ships at Troy.

popCulture.title: Thessalus
popCulture.description: Son of Heracles and king of Cos — father of the Homeric Coan leaders, distinct from Jason's son of the same name.
